summary: Michelle C. Wang works in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and history and archaeology. She completed her doctoral studies under Eugene Y. Wang circa 2002–2008 and became an assistant professor of art and art history at Georgetown University circa 2012.

Michelle Spuler is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies who earned her PhD at the University of Queensland (~1996–2000). She taught at Colorado College and later at Victoria University of Wellington in the Department of Religious Studies (~2001–2004).

Michiel de Vaan specializes in linguistics and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He completed his doctoral studies under Alexander Lubotsky (~1997–2002) and held a post at Leiden University from circa 2002 to 2014.

Michihiko Komine is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Taisho University. He served there as an assistant circa 1978 and later as professor (attested 2014–2015), as well as head of the Japanese Association for Esoteric Buddhist Studies (attested 2015).

Michihiko Yajima works in Indology and linguistics. A graduate student at the University of Tokyo (attested 1981), he held a post there (attested 1992) and later served as professor at Tsurumi University (attested 2003–2008).

Michihiro Ikeda is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He held teaching posts at Setagaya Gakuen High School (attested 1996) and Komazawa Junior College (attested 2005), and served as a librarian at the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies (attested 2005–2006).

Michiko Yusa is a scholar of religious studies, philosophy, and Japanology. She earned her PhD at the University of California, Santa Barbara under Raimon Panikkar (~1976–1983) and served as professor of foreign languages at Western Washington University (~1983–2019).
Michio Kamikawa specializes in history and archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Japanology. He studied at Ritsumeikan University and held a post at Aichi Prefectural University (attested 2016).

Michio Yano works in Indology and history and archaeology. He studied at Kyoto University (PhD 1996) under Kiyoshi Yabuuchi and at Brown University under David Pingree. He lectured at Kyoto University and was a professor at Kyoto Sangyo University (1973–2015).

Michitoshi Barada works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied under Jien Abe and J. R. Joshi, as well as at Savitribai Phule Pune University (1997), and held posts at Otani University (1992) and the Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute (2000–2003).
Michiya Ito was a graduate student at Tohoku University (attested 1990) and later held posts there (attested 1990 and 2001–2004).
Michiyo Demoto works in Buddhist studies and Indology. She studied at Kyoto University and held a post at the University of Marburg (attested 2024).
Michiyo Hoshi is a scholar of Tibetology and linguistics. She held posts at the Research Institute for Languages and Cultures of Asia and Africa and at Toyo Bunko (attested 2003).
Midori Nishino works in Buddhist studies and Indology. She completed doctoral studies at Taisho University (attested 2006), where she later served as a researcher (attested 2010–2015).
Mieko Kajihara is an Indologist who completed a PhD at Harvard University by 2002, having studied under Michael Witzel (attested 1997).

Migmar Tsering was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied under Khenpo Appey Rinpoche. He served as Sa skya expert at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies (attested 1990) and Head of Sakya College (attested 1991–1997).

Mihai Șora was a philosopher who studied at the University of Bucharest under Mircea Eliade (~1934–1938), the University of Paris (~1939–1947), and the CNRS (~1945–1948). He held a post at the State Publishing House for Literature and Arts until 1969.

Mikaël Bauer specializes in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He studied at Kanazawa University under Paul Hoornaert and Noritoshi Aramaki, and earned a PhD at Harvard University under Ryuichi Abe (attested 2010).

Mikel Burley specializes in Indology, philosophy, and religious studies. He studied at the University of Essex, under Jonardon Ganeri and Brian Carr, and earned his PhD at the University of Bristol under John Peacock. He served at the University of Leeds (2007–2020).
Mikio Otsuki works in Buddhist studies and Japanology. In 2007, he is attested as a professor at Hanazono University and a research fellow at Manpuku-ji.
